title: Dyninst on the RISC-V: Binary Instrumentation in Support of Performance, Debugging, and Other Tools
problem: Binary instrumentation tools like Dyninst are not yet available for the RISC-V architecture, limiting the ability to profile, debug, and analyze programs on RISC-V systems without access to source code.
method: Port the Dyninst binary instrumentation toolkit to the RISC-V architecture, addressing RISC-V-specific challenges in binary parsing, instruction manipulation, and relocation handling.

title: LEMOE: LLM-Enhanced Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Microarchitecture Exploration
problem: Design space exploration for processor microarchitecture is challenging due to vast design space and multiple competing metrics; traditional algorithm-driven approaches cannot effectively incorporate expert domain knowledge.
method: Uses LLM to enhance implicit Bayesian model for multi-objective optimization; features program-aware warm-up phase utilizing LLM and LLVM to produce initial design set with rich prior knowledge; leverages LLM contextual learning to improve surrogate modeling under sparse data.

title: 5.7 A 4.7GHz, 27.7dBm Pout, 37.8% PAE, 5.8° AM-PM Distortion Polar SCPA Using In-Cell Fast Slope-to-Phase Self-Calibration and Asymmetrical 4-to-1 Differential Power-Combining Transformer
problem: Digital power amplifiers (DPAs) for sub-6G and WiFi applications require high output power, high efficiency, and low linearity distortion to support complex modulation (high-order QAM). Conventional DPAs need additional digital pre-distortion (DPD) modules increasing area and power consumption. Voltage-mode switched-capacitor power amplifiers (SCPAs) improve linearity but suffer AM-PM (amplitude-to-phase) distortion at high frequencies due to transistor switching delays affecting waveform shape and phase response.
method: A polar switched-capacitor power amplifier (SCPA) with in-cell fast slope-to-phase self-calibration. Key techniques: (1) Edge detectors in each unit cell detect rising/falling edge delays in switching waveforms, (2) Slope-to-phase tuner adjusts edges in real-time to compensate for phase distortion, (3) Asymmetrical 4-to-1 differential power-combining transformer balancing impedance and efficiency, (4) Fast calibration loop (low loop delay) enabling sub-modulation-period response for wideband signal support.

title: Spatial-Temporal Direct-Digital Beamforming Power Amplifier with Enhanced Back-Off Efficiency in a 24GHz Phased Array
problem: mm-Wave transmitters face degraded back-off efficiency when transmitting high-order constellations (PAPR 7-9.5dB for 5G+) while requiring efficient beamforming. Traditional architectures address beamforming and power back-off (PBO) separately—baseband beamforming increases complexity; RF beamforming suffers mismatch and insertion loss.
method: The Spatial-Temporal Beamforming Power Amplifier (ST-BPA) integrates direct-digital amplitude-and-phase beamforming with power back-off operation in a unified mm-wave PA architecture. This combined approach can be augmented with efficiency-enhancement techniques (Doherty, envelope tracking, or outphasing) to further improve back-off performance across the phased array.

title: Is it an HPC Workflow Assistant? Is it a Framework? It's Drona Workflow Engine
problem: HPC resources increasingly complex; novice researchers face steep learning curve due to lack of HPC skills; inefficient resource utilization
method: GUI-based workflow assistant that generates HPC scripts; editable preview window for user control; flexible framework for importing/creating/sharing workflows

title: 3D-Flow: Flow-based Standard Cell Legalization for 3D ICs
problem: Standard-cell placement legalization in 3D ICs must resolve overflows across multiple dies while minimizing cell displacement; traditional 2D legalizers are inefficient for 3D geometry.
method: Proposes 3D-Flow, a flow-based legalization algorithm that models the 3D space as a grid graph and finds shortest augmenting paths to resolve overflowed bins; uses branch-and-bound for path optimization and cycle-canceling post-optimization to minimize maximum displacement.

title: Automated MCQA Benchmarking at Scale: Evaluating Reasoning Traces as Retrieval Sources for Domain Adaptation of Small Language Models
problem: Scientific knowledge grows rapidly, but evaluation benchmarks lag behind. Traditional benchmarks become stale. Small language models lack domain-specific knowledge without fine-tuning or retrieval augmentation.
method: Scalable pipeline automating MCQA generation from scientific paper corpora: PDF parsing, semantic chunking, question generation, model evaluation. Case study: 16,000+ MCQs from 22,000 papers in radiation and cancer biology. Evaluation of small LMs (1.1B-14B) with RAG using paper chunks vs. reasoning traces from GPT-4.

title: ALLMod: Exploring Area-Efficiency of LUT-based Large Number Modular Reduction via Hybrid Workloads
problem: Cryptographic applications (homomorphic encryption, zero-knowledge proofs) require high-bit-width modular reduction (128–8192 bits), which is compute-intensive. LUT-based approaches reduce computation via lookup tables but incur significant hardware area overhead due to extensive LUT storage.
method: ALLMod improves area efficiency of LUT-based modular reduction by employing hybrid workloads: decomposes the bit-group segmentation into two distinct workloads (inspired by iterative reduction), balances their distribution via a template, and uses design space exploration to find optimal timing for fusing results. Trades computation across workloads to reduce LUT storage while maintaining throughput.

title: TB-STC: Transposable Block-wise N:M Structured Sparse Tensor Core
problem: Existing N:M structured sparsity for DNN accelerators causes significant accuracy degradation (e.g., >6% on OPT-6.7B and Llama2-7B at 50% sparsity) because one-dimensional structured sparsity patterns diverge far from the unstructured optimal. Hardware support for sparsity must simultaneously deliver high bandwidth utilization and computational efficiency.
method: The paper introduces Transposable Block-wise Structured (TBS) sparsity, which exploits the transpose relationship between forward and backward pass weight matrices during training to find a 2D block sparsity pattern that more closely approximates unstructured sparsity. At the micro-architecture level, TB-STC implements a Transposable Block-wise N:M Sparse Tensor Core with an adaptive codec for on-the-fly storage format conversion supporting both row-wise and column-wise sparse access, and an I/O-aware configurable scheduler for sparsity-aware compute scheduling. This enables 1.47x bandwidth utilization and 1.57x computational utilization improvements.

title: A 38.1Mb/mm2 SRAM in a 2nm-CMOS-Nanosheet Technology for High-Density and Energy-Efficient Compute
problem: Scaling SRAM bit-cell area at advanced nodes faces diminishing returns; peripheral circuits dominate area overhead, and maintaining reliability at reduced cell voltage becomes challenging.
method: Design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) leveraging 2nm nanosheet technology's improved on/off-current ratio to increase BL loading capacity by 2x, allowing denser memory bit arrays per peripheral circuit. Special logic rules and floor-planning techniques optimize both cell and peripheral area while maintaining reliability margins.

title: Usability Evaluation of Cloud for HPC Applications
problem: Unclear whether cloud environments (Azure, AWS, GCP) provide equivalent performance and usability for HPC workloads compared to on-premises HPC clusters.
method: Cross-platform usability study: 11 HPC proxy apps/benchmarks across 3 clouds, 6 environments, CPU/GPU configs, scaling to 28,672 CPUs and 256 GPUs, benchmarked against LLNL on-premises clusters.

title: An MLIR pipeline for offloading Fortran to FPGAs via OpenMP
problem: HPC applications written in Fortran lack efficient pathways for offloading compute kernels to FPGAs for acceleration, requiring custom compilers and limiting portability.
method: MLIR-based compiler pipeline combining OpenMP dialect with High-Level Synthesis (HLS) dialect. Flang frontend parses Fortran; MLIR transforms code; HLS backend targets FPGA synthesis. Supports OpenMP target directives for selective offloading and manual kernel optimization.

title: SIGMo: High-Throughput Batched Subgraph Isomorphism on GPUs for Molecular Matching
problem: Subgraph isomorphism is NP-complete and computationally expensive; state-of-the-art frameworks insufficient for large-scale molecular matching
method: SYCL-based portable GPU framework with multi-level iterative filtering using neighborhood signature encoding; stack-based DFS join phase

title: McPAL: Scaling Unstructured Sparse Inference with Multi-Chiplet HBM-PIM Architecture for LLMs
problem: Monolithic PIM architectures cannot scale to very large LLMs (70B+) due to single-die memory footprint limits; LLM inference is memory-bound, and PIM can provide high memory bandwidth but scaling via larger dies hits power/yield constraints.
method: Multi-chiplet HBM-PIM architecture (McPAL) that decomposes arbitrary unstructured sparse weight matrices into multiple irregular sparse vectors, then routes non-skipped computations via in-memory butterfly network to standard PIM arrays. Vertically scales via 3D-HBM hierarchy (minimizing long-distance data travel) and horizontally via 2.5D IO chiplet (reducing die-to-die traffic and balancing sparse workload).

title: D-VSync: Decoupled Rendering and Displaying for Smartphone Graphics
problem: The VSync-based rendering architecture on smartphones tightly couples the rendering pipeline to the display refresh cycle, causing frame drops and increased rendering latency when large high-frame-rate screens and complex visual effects (physics-based animations, stunning UI) demand rendering time that exceeds the VSync interval. This rigid coupling prevents flexible scheduling of rendering work across display periods.
method: D-VSync decouples the rendering pipeline from the display refresh cycle by separating the rendering scheduler from the VSync signal, allowing rendering to be completed asynchronously relative to display timing. The system introduces a buffering and synchronization layer that permits rendering jobs to run beyond a single VSync period and uses predictive scheduling to align rendered frames with the nearest available display window, reducing the frequency of missed frames.

title: A Study on the Impact of Temperature-Dependent Ferroelectric Switching Behavior in 3D Memory Architecture
problem: Hafnium Zirconium Oxide (HZO) FeRAM in 3D neural network accelerators suffers from thermal stress as on-chip temperatures rise during operation. Temperature-dependent ferroelectric switching behavior has not been well characterized in 3D memory architectures.
method: Experimental device characterization and circuit/architecture-level simulation of HZO-based FeRAM in 3D memory architectures. Study of temperature-dependent polarization switching behavior through thermal impact analysis. Dynamic write voltage optimization exploiting temperature-activated switching mechanisms.
